long_biography.plain_text:
Polygon Investment Partners brought Alexander Edward Jackson together with Reade Griffith and Paddy Dear as co-founders of a jointly owned investment manager. Jackson focused on convertible arbitrage, credit, capital-structure trades, structured credit and private investments. His remit also covered risk management and systems development, giving him a role in both portfolio judgment and the infrastructure behind it. The founders later helped establish Tetragon as a separate investment platform.

Jackson had begun at Paine Webber before joining Taylor & Company, where he handled Japanese equity-derivative investments. Nine years at Highbridge Capital Management followed. He supervised Asian and European convertible and credit books, contributed to the firm's American investment team and ultimately led its European office. A mathematics degree from Tufts and an MBA from Columbia complemented that market experience, which became the foundation for his work building investment firms.
